title: Session TTL shortened in auth module; cleanup job keeps the old constant and purges live sessions

base.jobs/cleanup.py:
import time

SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 7 * 24 * 3600


def purge(sessions):
    now = time.time()
    return [s for s in sessions if now - s['created'] < SESSION_TTL_SECONDS]

head.auth/session.py:
# security review: 7 days was too long
SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 12 * 3600


def expires_at(created):
    return created + SESSION_TTL_SECONDS
head.jobs/cleanup.py:
import time

SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 7 * 24 * 3600


def purge(sessions):
    now = time.time()
    return [s for s in sessions if now - s['created'] < SESSION_TTL_SECONDS]

labels.defect: TTL constant duplicated in two modules; only one was changed
labels.evidence: Sessions expire after 12h for auth but the cleanup job retains them for 7 days — expired-but-retained sessions remain resumable through any path that trusts the store.

labels.defect: Cleanup uses its own stale TTL copy instead of importing auth.session's
